newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Democrats press govt on gold sale probe.
newsitem.headline: Australian Democrats press govt on gold sale probe.

text.p: The small but influential Australian Democrats party said on Friday it would push for a separate parliamentary probe of the Reserve Bank's gold sales if the government blocked evidence before an existing committee.
Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot said she supported the Labor opposition's call for Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane to give evidence to the Senate economics committee.

But if the government sought to block that move, the Democrats would move to set up a separate committee to look at the A$2.4 billion sale of two thirds of the bank's gold reserves, she said in a statement.

Labor and the Democrats want the government-dominated economics committee to examine the sale and the involvement of WMC Ltd managing director and bank board member Hugh Morgan, at its meeting on August 18.
While the Liberal-National government can use its committee majority to block the bid, the government does not have a majority in parliament's upper house, the Senate.
Labor and the Democrats can combine with other minority parties and independents to force a separate inquiry after parliament resumes on August 25.
"With public focus clearly on conflict of interest matters at the moment, it's appropriate for the RBA's decision to be given proper scrutiny," Kernot said.
"The (economics) committee should examine whether the RBA board's secrecy amd disclosure rules are adequate to deal with potential or real conflicts of interest."
The bank announced early this month it had sold 167 tonnes of gold reserves in staged sales over the previous six months.
The announcement was blamed for contributing to a fall in the gold price to a 12-year low.
But the government has defended the sale as prudent and in the national interests, with the proceeds reinvested in interest-bearing foreign currency investments.
Morgan has denied any conflict of interest or passing on any information gained as a board member to his company or its executives.
